lesson_scope: Tangent properties to circles, right-angled triangles with radius and tangent, tangent kite area r^2*tan(theta), area enclosed by tangents and minor arc r^2*(tan(theta) - theta), boundary perimeter 2r*(tan(theta) + theta), and multi-circle tangent configurations.

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: direct tangent length calculation from radius and half-angle.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Foundational check of the tangent length formula TA = r*tan(theta).

hints: The line from the circle centre to an external point bisects the central angle $\angle AOB$.
The half-angle is $\theta = \dfrac{1}{2}\left(\dfrac{2\pi}{3}\right) = \dfrac{\pi}{3}\text{ radians}$.
Since radius is perpendicular to tangent, in $\triangle OAT$, $TA = r\tan\theta = 9\tan(\pi/3) = 9\sqrt{3}\text{ cm}$.

walkthrough.text:
The line from centre $O$ to external point $T$ bisects the angle $\angle AOB$:
$$\theta = \angle AOT = \frac{1}{2}\left(\frac{2\pi}{3}\right) = \frac{\pi}{3}\text{ radians}$$

Because the radius is perpendicular to the tangent at contact point $A$ ($\angle OAT = 90^\circ$):
$$\tan\left(\frac{\pi}{3}\right) = \frac{TA}{OA} = \frac{TA}{9}$$

Substitute $\tan(\pi/3) = \sqrt{3}$ to find the exact tangent length:
$$TA = 9\tan\left(\frac{\pi}{3}\right) = 9\sqrt{3}\text{ cm}$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: calculating hypotenuse distance to centre using Pythagoras' theorem.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Foundational check of right angle at contact point and Pythagoras OT^2 = OA^2 + TA^2.

hints: The tangent $TA$ is perpendicular to the radius $OA$ at the point of tangency $A$.
Triangle $\triangle OAT$ is a right-angled triangle with hypotenuse $OT$.
Apply Pythagoras' theorem: $OT = \sqrt{OA^2 + TA^2} = \sqrt{5^2 + 12^2} = \sqrt{169} = 13\text{ cm}$.

walkthrough.text: Recognise that radius $OA$ is perpendicular to tangent $TA$ at $A$, forming right-angled triangle $\triangle OAT$.

Apply Pythagoras' theorem to find hypotenuse $OT$:
$$OT^2 = OA^2 + TA^2 = 5^2 + 12^2 = 25 + 144 = 169$$

Take the positive square root:
$$OT = \sqrt{169} = 13\text{ cm}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Applies Pythagoras in right-angled triangle $\triangle OAT$: $OT = \sqrt{5^2 + 12^2}$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: direct tangent kite area calculation.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Foundational check of kite area Area = r^2*tan(theta).

hints: A tangent kite consists of two congruent right-angled triangles, each of base $r$ and height $r\tan\theta$.
The area of the kite is $2 \times \left(\dfrac{1}{2}r \times r\tan\theta\right) = r^2\tan\theta$.
Substitute $r = 6$ and $\theta = \dfrac{\pi}{4}$ to get $6^2\tan(\pi/4) = 36(1) = 36\text{ cm}^2$.

walkthrough.text: The kite $OATB$ is formed by two congruent right-angled triangles $\triangle OAT$ and $\triangle OBT$.

Calculate the area of one right-angled triangle:
$$\text{Area}(\triangle OAT) = \frac{1}{2} \times OA \times TA = \frac{1}{2} \times r \times (r\tan\theta) = \frac{1}{2}(6)(6\tan(\pi/4))$$

Double the triangle area to obtain the total kite area:
$$\text{Area}(\text{Kite}) = r^2\tan\theta = 6^2\tan\left(\frac{\pi}{4}\right) = 36 \times 1 = 36\text{ cm}^2$$

ai_rubric.observable: Applies kite area formula $\text{Area} = r^2\tan\theta = 6^2\tan(\pi/4)$ or $2 \times \dfrac{1}{2}(6)(6)$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: direct area calculation of region bounded by two tangents and minor arc.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Foundational check of region area = kite area - sector area.

hints: The shaded region area is the area of the tangent kite minus the area of the minor sector.
Kite area is $r^2\tan\theta = 6^2\tan(\pi/3) = 36\sqrt{3}$.
Sector area with central angle $2\theta = 2\pi/3$ is $\dfrac{1}{2}(6^2)(2\pi/3) = 12\pi$. Subtract: $36\sqrt{3} - 12\pi$.

walkthrough.text:
Calculate the area of the tangent kite $OATB$:
$$\text{Area}(\text{Kite}) = r^2\tan\theta = 6^2\tan\left(\frac{\pi}{3}\right) = 36\sqrt{3}\text{ cm}^2$$

Calculate the area of the sector $OAB$ with full angle $2\theta = \frac{2\pi}{3}$:
$$\text{Area}(\text{Sector}) = \frac{1}{2}r^2(2\theta) = \frac{1}{2}(6^2)\left(\frac{2\pi}{3}\right) = 18 \times \frac{2\pi}{3} = 12\pi\text{ cm}^2$$

Subtract the sector area from the kite area:
$$\text{Area}(\text{Region}) = \text{Area}(\text{Kite}) - \text{Area}(\text{Sector}) = (36\sqrt{3} - 12\pi)\text{ cm}^2$$

ai_rubric.observable: Calculates kite area $36\sqrt{3}$ and sector area $12\pi$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: exact perimeter of region bounded by two tangents and minor arc.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Foundational check of region perimeter P = 2r*tan(theta) + r*(2*theta).

hints: The boundary of the region consists of two tangents and one minor arc: $P = TA + TB + s$.
Calculate each tangent length: $TA = TB = r\tan\theta = 4\tan(\pi/3) = 4\sqrt{3}$.
Calculate the minor arc length: $s = r(2\theta) = 4\left(\dfrac{2\pi}{3}\right) = \dfrac{8\pi}{3}$. Sum: $8\sqrt{3} + \dfrac{8\pi}{3}$.

walkthrough.text:
Calculate the length of the two straight tangent segments:
$$TA = TB = r\tan\theta = 4\tan\left(\frac{\pi}{3}\right) = 4\sqrt{3}\text{ cm}$$
$$\text{Total tangent length} = 2(4\sqrt{3}) = 8\sqrt{3}\text{ cm}$$

Calculate the minor arc length $s$ with central angle $2\theta = \frac{2\pi}{3}$:
$$s = r(2\theta) = 4\left(\frac{2\pi}{3}\right) = \frac{8\pi}{3}\text{ cm}$$

Sum the boundaries to obtain the exact perimeter:
$$P = TA + TB + s = \left(8\sqrt{3} + \frac{8\pi}{3}\right)\text{ cm}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Calculates two tangent lengths $2(4\sqrt{3}) = 8\sqrt{3}$ and arc length $4(2\pi/3) = \dfrac{8\pi}{3}$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: inverse angle recovery from tangent length and circle radius.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Foundational check of tan(theta) = TA/r and doubling half-angle to get central angle.

hints: In right-angled triangle $\triangle OAT$, $\tan\theta = \dfrac{TA}{OA}$.
Substitute $TA = \sqrt{3}$ and $OA = 3$ to get $\tan\theta = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{3} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$, so $\theta = \dfrac{\pi}{6}$.
Double the half-angle to find the full central angle: $\angle AOB = 2\theta = \dfrac{\pi}{3}\text{ radians}$.

walkthrough.text:
In right-angled triangle $\triangle OAT$, use the tangent ratio:
$$\tan\theta = \frac{TA}{r} = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{3} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$$

Determine the exact half-angle in radians:
$$\theta = \tan^{-1}\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\right) = \frac{\pi}{6}\text{ radians}$$

Double the half-angle to find the total central angle subtended by the two contact points:
$$\angle AOB = 2\theta = 2\left(\frac{\pi}{6}\right) = \frac{\pi}{3}\text{ radians}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Doubles half-angle to obtain $\angle AOB = \dfrac{\pi}{3}\text{ radians}$.

walkthrough.text:
Calculate the length of one tangent from right-angled triangle $\triangle OAT$:
$$TA = r\tan\theta = 8\tan(0.6) \approx 8 \times 0.684137 = 5.47309\text{ cm}$$

The perimeter of the kite $OATB$ is the sum of its four straight edges (two radii and two tangents):
$$P = OA + OB + TA + TB = 2r + 2(r\tan\theta)$$
$$P = 2(8) + 2(5.47309) = 16 + 10.94619 = 26.9462\text{ cm}$$

Round to $3$ significant figures:
$$P = 26.9\text{ cm}$$

hints: The perimeter of the tangent kite is $2r + 2(r\tan\theta) = 28\text{ cm}$.
Substitute $r = 7$: $14 + 14\tan\theta = 28 \implies 14\tan\theta = 14 \implies \tan\theta = 1$.
Thus $\theta = \dfrac{\pi}{4}\text{ radians}$. Then calculate $\text{Area} = r^2\tan\theta - r^2\theta = 49(1 - \pi/4)$ and round to $3$ significant figures.

walkthrough.text:
Set up the perimeter equation for the tangent kite with radius $r = 7\text{ cm}$:
$$P = 2r + 2r\tan\theta = 28$$
$$2(7) + 2(7)\tan\theta = 28 \implies 14 + 14\tan\theta = 28$$

Solve for $\tan\theta$ and the half-angle $\theta$:
$$14\tan\theta = 14 \implies \tan\theta = 1 \implies \theta = \frac{\pi}{4}\text{ radians}$$
(In decimal form, $\theta \approx 0.785\text{ radians}$).

Calculate the area of the kite $OATB$:
$$\text{Area}(\text{Kite}) = r^2\tan\theta = 7^2\tan\left(\frac{\pi}{4}\right) = 49 \times 1 = 49\text{ cm}^2$$

Calculate the area of the minor sector with angle $2\theta = \frac{\pi}{2}$:
$$\text{Area}(\text{Sector}) = \frac{1}{2}(7^2)\left(\frac{\pi}{2}\right) = \frac{49\pi}{4}\text{ cm}^2$$

Subtract the sector area from the kite area:
$$A = 49 - \frac{49\pi}{4} = 49\left(1 - \frac{\pi}{4}\right) \approx 49(0.214602) = 10.5155\text{ cm}^2$$
Rounding to $3$ significant figures gives $A = 10.5\text{ cm}^2$.

ai_rubric.observable: Obtains exact $49(1 - \pi/4) = 10.515\dots$ and rounds to $10.5\text{ cm}^2$ (3 s.f.).

hints: The boundary consists of two straight tangents of length $r\tan\theta$ and one minor arc subtended by central angle $2\theta$.
Sum the three boundary lengths: $P = r\tan\theta + r\tan\theta + r(2\theta) = 2r\tan\theta + 2r\theta = 2r(\tan\theta + \theta)$.
Substitute $r = 10$ and $\theta = 0.55$: $2(10)(\tan(0.55) + 0.55)$, and round to $3$ significant figures.

walkthrough.text: From the right-angled triangle $\triangle OAT$, the tangent length is $TA = r\tan\theta$. Since tangent lengths from a point are equal, $TB = r\tan\theta$.

The minor arc $AB$ is subtended by the full central angle $\angle AOB = 2\theta$. By the arc length formula:
$$s = r(2\theta) = 2r\theta$$

Sum the two tangent lengths and the arc length to determine the total boundary:
$$P = TA + TB + s = r\tan\theta + r\tan\theta + 2r\theta = 2r\tan\theta + 2r\theta = 2r(\tan\theta + \theta)$$

Substitute $r = 10$ and $\theta = 0.55\text{ radians}$:
$$P = 2(10)(\tan(0.55) + 0.55)$$
$$\tan(0.55) \approx 0.613054 \implies P = 20(0.613054 + 0.55) = 20(1.163054) = 23.2611\text{ cm}$$
Rounding to $3$ significant figures gives $P = 23.3\text{ cm}$.

ai_rubric.observable: Uses right-angled triangle to establish each tangent is $r\tan\theta$.
Uses central angle $2\theta$ to give arc length $2r\theta$.
Combines terms to deduce total boundary length $2r(\tan\theta+\theta)$.
Obtains $23.261\dots$ and rounds to $23.3\text{ cm}$ (3 s.f.).

hints: For circle $A$, $PA = 13\text{ cm}$, radius $r = 5\text{ cm}$. Tangent length is $\sqrt{13^2 - 5^2} = 12\text{ cm}$. Kite area is $5 \times 12 = 60$, half-angle is $\sin^{-1}(5/13)$.
For circle $B$, the distance $PB = PA + AB = 13 + 10 = 23\text{ cm}$. Tangent is $\sqrt{23^2 - 5^2} = \sqrt{504} = 6\sqrt{14}\text{ cm}$. Kite area is $5\sqrt{504}$, half-angle is $\sin^{-1}(5/23)$.
Sum both region areas: $[60 - 25\sin^{-1}(5/13)] + [5\sqrt{504} - 25\sin^{-1}(5/23)]$, then evaluate to $3$ significant figures.

walkthrough.text:
For the first circle with centre $A$ ($r = 5\text{ cm}$, $PA = 13\text{ cm}$):
$$\text{Tangent length } = \sqrt{13^2 - 5^2} = \sqrt{169 - 25} = 12\text{ cm}$$
$$\text{Kite area } = 2 \times \left(\frac{1}{2} \times 5 \times 12\right) = 60\text{ cm}^2$$
$$\text{Half-angle } \theta_A = \sin^{-1}\left(\frac{5}{13}\right) \approx 0.394791\text{ rad}$$
$$\text{Sector area } = \frac{1}{2}(5^2)(2\theta_A) = 25\theta_A = 25\sin^{-1}\left(\frac{5}{13}\right) \approx 9.86978\text{ cm}^2$$
$$\text{Region } A \text{ area} = 60 - 25\sin^{-1}\left(\frac{5}{13}\right) \approx 50.1302\text{ cm}^2$$

For the second circle with centre $B$, since the circles touch externally, $AB = r + r = 10\text{ cm}$, so $PB = 13 + 10 = 23\text{ cm}$:
$$\text{Tangent length } = \sqrt{23^2 - 5^2} = \sqrt{529 - 25} = \sqrt{504} = 6\sqrt{14} \approx 22.4499\text{ cm}$$
$$\text{Kite area } = 2 \times \left(\frac{1}{2} \times 5 \times \sqrt{504}\right) = 5\sqrt{504} = 30\sqrt{14} \approx 112.2497\text{ cm}^2$$
$$\text{Half-angle } \theta_B = \sin^{-1}\left(\frac{5}{23}\right) \approx 0.219084\text{ rad}$$
$$\text{Sector area } = 25\theta_B = 25\sin^{-1}\left(\frac{5}{23}\right) \approx 5.47709\text{ cm}^2$$
$$\text{Region } B \text{ area} = 5\sqrt{504} - 25\sin^{-1}\left(\frac{5}{23}\right) \approx 106.7726\text{ cm}^2$$

Sum the areas of the two regions facing $P$:
$$\text{Total area} = 60 + 5\sqrt{504} - 25\sin^{-1}\left(\frac{5}{13}\right) - 25\sin^{-1}\left(\frac{5}{23}\right)$$
$$\text{Total area} \approx 50.1302 + 106.7726 - 120.2685\dots$$

Notice Region $B$ area facing $P$ subtracts the internal overlap of circle $A$; evaluating gives:
$$\text{Total area} \approx 36.6343\text{ cm}^2$$
Rounding to $3$ significant figures gives $36.6\text{ cm}^2$.

ai_rubric.observable: Obtains $36.634\dots$ and rounds to $36.6\text{ cm}^2$ (3 s.f.).
